channel.title: Civilizational-Transition on Pivtorak.Studio
channel.description: Recent content in Civilizational-Transition on Pivtorak.Studio

item.title: 02-03 AfterTragedy. The Illusion of a Game
item.description: The work examines the illusion of political participation inside authoritarian regimes, where procedures become theatrical instruments masking predetermined outcomes and systemic repression.

item.title: 03-01 Diagnosis of the System. Vertical of Fear
item.description: This work diagnoses the architecture of fear inside authoritarian regimes, revealing how coercive hierarchies consume their own participants and ultimately become structurally fragile.

item.title: 03-02 Diagnosis of the System. Resource Dependence
item.description: This work diagnoses the parasitic architecture of tyranny, revealing how resource extraction, coercion, and dependency on external flows become the primary conditions of regime survival.

item.title: 03-03 Diagnosis of the System. Imitation of State
item.description: This work diagnoses the decorative architecture of tyranny, exposing how courts, ministries, and laws become props that conceal the absence of governance, accountability, and public service.

item.title: 04-01 Vulnerability Point. Human Factor
item.description: This work diagnoses the fragility of authoritarian regimes through the conscience of their executors. Even the most disciplined apparatus cannot fully suppress humanity. A single moment of doubt may become the beginning of systemic collapse.

item.title: 04-02 Vulnerability Point. Economic Overload
item.description: This work diagnoses the economic overload of authoritarian rule. Repression consumes resources without creating value, and the regime gradually exhausts its own foundations. Tyranny eventually becomes more expensive than society can sustain.

item.title: 04-03 Vulnerability Point. Informational Fragility
item.description: This work diagnoses the informational vulnerability of authoritarian rule. Propaganda survives only while reality cannot be compared. Once people regain access to independent sources of truth, the ideological façade begins to collapse.

item.title: 06-01 Desacralization of Fear. Exposing Vulnerability
item.description: This work documents the desacralization of fear as a civilizational turning point. A trembling hand reflected in a puddle exposes the hidden fragility of authoritarian violence and reveals that repressive systems are sustained by circulating fear rather than genuine strength.

item.title: 06-02 Desacralization of Fear. Loss of Subjectivity
item.description: This work documents the dissolution of authoritarian subjectivity as a civilizational turning point. An empty office, fading symbols, and weightless orders reveal that dictatorship exists only while people participate in its relational network.

item.title: 06-03 Desacralization of Fear. Inevitability of Tribunal
item.description: This work documents the final stage of the desacralization of fear. Prison bars become legal protocols, victims become witnesses, and dictatorship loses its ability to conceal violence as history itself begins to register every act.

item.title: 08-01 Point of Transition. Request for a Bridge (Pahlavi)
item.description: After the collapse of fear and the restoration of identity, Persia faces a dangerous vacuum. This work explores Pahlavi as a mechanism of continuity that connects the memory of Cyrus the Great with modern democratic institutions, allowing the transition from tyranny to democracy without structural collapse.
